narrativeReportMd:
# ResearchElementDefinition R4-to-R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
`ResearchElementDefinition` is a hard breaking removal in the supplied R6 ballot package. R4 instances with `resourceType: "ResearchElementDefinition"`, generated model classes, profiles, references, and validators have no same-identity R6 resource to target.

## Scope
The assessment used the R4 StructureDefinition, the absent R6 path, both package indexes and metadata, R6 `fhir-old-types`, selected local terminology, and R4/R6 `EvidenceVariable` as a candidate migration destination. Base-resource and infrastructure changes are excluded.

## Main migration themes
Migration is not a field rename. R4 `ResearchElementDefinition` centers on a required `type` (`population`, `exposure`, `outcome`) and at least one required `characteristic.definition[x]`. R6 `EvidenceVariable` instead models variable meaning through optional `definition`, `definitionModifier`, `handling`, `category`, `conditional`, `dataStorage`, `timing`, `period`, `constraint`, and missing/unacceptable-data elements. Several R4 metadata fields also disappear or change shape.

## Highest-impact findings
The root resource removal is the primary hard validation break. The next highest risks are the absence of a lossless successor mapping, the removal of the required PICO `type` classification, and the replacement of the mandatory `characteristic` backbone.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is needed for the mapping from R4 `type`, `variableType`, `characteristic.definition[x]`, exclusion semantics, timing fields, UCUM unit fields, and group-measure fields into R6. The local package did not include an official ConceptMap or migration guide.

## Backward-compatible design observations
Because R4 `ResearchElementDefinition` was draft/trial-use, retirement may be justified by evidence-domain redesign. A less disruptive approach would have retained a deprecated R6 StructureDefinition, shipped aliases or cross-version extensions for old fields, or provided an authoritative conversion map.

## Follow-up analysis
Coordinate with the `EvidenceVariable`, `Evidence`, and `ResearchDefinition` reports and with terminology mapping work for research-element-type, variable-type, group-measure, UCUM, and EvidenceVariable handling/classifier value sets.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: `ResearchElementDefinition` is not present as an R6 resource. Top migration concerns are: existing R4 instances fail at the resource-type level; the likely `EvidenceVariable` successor is not a one-to-one rename; and R4's required PICO `type` plus mandatory `characteristic` model require semantic remapping. The main uncertainty is the absence of an official ConceptMap or migration narrative.
summary.migrationThemesMd: R4-to-R6 migration must choose a new evidence-domain representation, most plausibly involving R6 `EvidenceVariable` and sometimes `Evidence`, `Group`, or extensions. A mechanical `resourceType` replacement will not work because old fields such as `type`, `variableType`, `characteristic`, `subject[x]`, `usage`, `library`, and parts of `relatedArtifact` have no same-path R6 target. R6-to-R4 round-tripping is also risky because R6 EvidenceVariable permits instances without R4-required `status`, `type`, or `characteristic`, and it can express data-storage, constraint, and missing-data semantics that R4 ResearchElementDefinition cannot carry.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high that the same-name R6 artifact is absent: the assigned file is missing, the R6 package index has no StructureDefinition entry, and `fhir-old-types` identifies the name as old. Confidence is medium for exact replacement guidance because `EvidenceVariable` is only a candidate successor inferred from local definitions and purpose text, not an official ConceptMap. Terminology and semantic confidence would improve with official expansions and migration notes.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The same canonical artifact is absent in R6. The R6 old-types terminology entry confirms this is an intentional old resource name rather than merely a missing local file.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a direct validation and runtime break. An R4 JSON or XML instance with `resourceType` `ResearchElementDefinition` has no corresponding R6 base resource definition, so strict validators, parsers, generated classes, schemas, REST resource-type switches, and CapabilityStatement declarations cannot treat it as a normal R6 resource.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The resource was trial-use and likely uncommon in broad exchange, but it can carry evidence or recommendation semantics. Losing it without a reviewed mapping can change the meaning of knowledge artifacts that distinguish populations, exposures, and outcomes.

justification.inferredGoal: Retire or merge a draft PICO element resource into the newer evidence-variable model.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain a deprecated R6 ResearchElementDefinition resource with the R4 shape while steering new content to EvidenceVariable.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The apparent goal, retiring or merging a draft/FMM 0 PICO resource into the R6 evidence-variable model, is reasonable. Complete removal is still a hard break, and the local inputs do not include the official rationale. A base R6 compatibility resource could have reduced much of the breakage, but it would also require validators, servers, code generators, search surfaces, and documentation to keep supporting an obsolete trial-use resource. Given that material long-term burden, the breaking design is probably justified rather than clearly avoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base design would have kept `ResearchElementDefinition` in R6 as a deprecated resource, with the R4-compatible shape and explicit guidance that new implementations should use `EvidenceVariable` or related evidence resources. That would preserve most existing R4 instances and generated types. A ConceptMap or conversion tool alone would be useful migration guidance, but it is not a backward-compatible base design alternative. The main downside is that two same-domain representations could persist indefinitely.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: This would preserve old instances, but it would keep a duplicate draft evidence-domain resource alive and risk indefinite parallel representations.

findings.narrativeMd: The resource identity itself disappeared. This is more disruptive than an element rename because all instance payloads, generated classes, profiles, canonical references, search parameters, and server resource registries that mention `ResearchElementDefinition` need a new target model before they can operate against R6.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4-valid `ResearchElementDefinition` instance becomes R6-invalid at the resource-type level. The failure happens before element-level validation: a strict R6 validator or parser cannot select a base StructureDefinition for the resource. There is no same-identity R6 instance to round-trip back to R4, so the direct R6-to-R4 question is not applicable for this root finding.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Inventory stored instances, references, profiles, search parameters, generated code, and CapabilityStatements that use `ResearchElementDefinition`. Select an explicit replacement pattern, likely involving R6 `EvidenceVariable` and sometimes `Evidence`, `Group`, or extensions. Test at least minimal R4 instances, instances with all characteristic timing fields, and instances referenced from `ResearchDefinition` or knowledge artifacts.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Removal may be reasonable for a draft trial-use artifact, but it is not backward compatible. A deprecated resource shell, formal ConceptMap, or cross-version extension package would have reduced validation and code-generation disruption while still allowing the evidence domain to converge on R6 `EvidenceVariable`.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 `ResearchElementDefinition` instances cannot validate or route as R6 resources because the same-name StructureDefinition is absent and R6 marks the name as an old FHIR type. That is a real resource-identity and generated-code break. The change still looks proportionate because the R4 artifact was FMM 0/trial-use, the R4 narrative pages themselves show very immature scope content, and keeping an obsolete resource in base R6 would force ongoing server, validator, search, and SDK support for a duplicate evidence-domain representation.
keyEvidence: R4 package contains `StructureDefinition-ResearchElementDefinition.json`; R6 package has no same-name file or package-index StructureDefinition entry.
R6 `CodeSystem-fhir-old-types` includes `ResearchElementDefinition` as an old resource name no longer used in this version.
R4 maturity map reports standardsStatus=trial-use and fmm=0.

R4 spec page `https://hl7.org/fhir/R4/researchelementdefinition.html` has TODO Scope/Boundaries text; examples page has only a TODO examples section. Quick web/GitHub checks found generated model support but no concrete production-exchange evidence.
freshReview.fmmEffect: R4 FMM 0 and trial-use status strongly soften the stability concern; the hard resource-type break remains real, but low maturity and lack of quick production-use evidence make removal less concerning than it would be for mature content.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: any R4 instance with `resourceType: ResearchElementDefinition` lacks a base R6 StructureDefinition, and generated model/server resource registries lose the type.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: R6 could have retained a deprecated compatibility resource with the R4 shape. That would preserve old payloads and SDK properties, but it would keep a duplicate, immature evidence resource alive and require ongoing search, validation, documentation, and implementation support; a ConceptMap alone would be migration guidance, not a less-breaking base design.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing High hard-break impact and Partial alternative judgment; the independent review gives more weight to FMM 0 and the cost of retaining a duplicate obsolete resource, so the final judgment is probably OK rather than a design revisit.

findings.title: Closest R6 successor is EvidenceVariable, but the match is semantic rather than a one-to-one rename

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The match is based on shared purpose text, evidence-domain context, and overlapping variable semantics. It is not high-confidence as an identity mapping because R4 had a separate `EvidenceVariable` and the local R6 package lacks an official ConceptMap or migration note.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The root removal is the direct validation break; this finding captures migration risk after selecting a replacement. If implementers assume a simple rename to `EvidenceVariable`, they can silently lose PICO role, characteristic, timing, library, or subject semantics. R6 `EvidenceVariable` can also express data-storage, constraints, and missing-data handling that R4 `ResearchElementDefinition` cannot represent.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Evidence-variable meaning can affect clinical research definitions and recommendation logic. An incorrect semantic mapping can change which population, exposure, or outcome a knowledge artifact is about.

justification.inferredGoal: Consolidate overlapping R4 evidence-domain resources into the R6 EvidenceVariable model.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep ResearchElementDefinition as a deprecated compatibility resource or explicit base compatibility alias during consolidation.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Consolidating overlapping evidence-domain resources into `EvidenceVariable` is a plausible R6 goal, and the report's evidence shows this is not a simple rename because R4 already had a distinct `EvidenceVariable`. The previous `Yes` alternative relied heavily on a formal ConceptMap or conversion profile, which is migration guidance rather than a less-breaking base model. A base compatibility resource could reduce the breakage, but only partially, because semantic review is still needed and duplicate representations would remain.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design would have retained `ResearchElementDefinition` as a deprecated R6 resource or provided a genuine base-level compatibility alias while declaring `EvidenceVariable` the preferred model. This would let old instances and generated code continue to validate while implementers migrated. A published ConceptMap, profile, or extension strategy would be valuable, but by itself it does not preserve R4-valid instances as R6 base instances.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: A compatibility shell would reduce inconsistent mappings, but it cannot make EvidenceVariable a true rename and would duplicate a redesigned evidence model.

examples.examplesMd: The migration example is illustrative only. The `classifier` text preserves the old PICO role, but no official value set or ConceptMap was found to make this lossless.

findings.narrativeMd: `EvidenceVariable` is the best local candidate successor, but treating it as a simple rename is unsafe. The two resources coexisted in R4, and the R6 resource uses a different content model. Implementers need explicit mapping rules rather than a global `resourceType` substitution.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: A same-identity R4 instance remains invalid in R6. If an implementation changes only `resourceType` to `EvidenceVariable`, mandatory R4 fields such as `type` and `characteristic` become unknown R6 elements, and R6 fields such as `dataStorage` or `constraint` cannot be represented back in R4 without extensions or loss.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Define a project-level mapping policy before converting data. Decide whether R4 `type` becomes `Evidence.variableDefinition.variableRole`, `EvidenceVariable.classifier`, an extension, or context supplied by the referencing resource. Preserve original canonical URLs and resource ids where possible, and add regression tests for population, exposure, comparator, and outcome cases.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The likely consolidation may be justified by a cleaner evidence model, but the lack of an explicit compatibility layer makes the migration policy-dependent. Backward-compatible aliases, conversion maps, or profiles would have reduced ambiguity without forcing the old model to remain the preferred R6 representation.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The closest inspected R6 resource, `EvidenceVariable`, shares purpose text with R4 `ResearchElementDefinition`, but it is not a clean rename because R4 already had a separate `EvidenceVariable` and R6 also uses `Evidence.variableDefinition` for variable roles. Without an official migration note or ConceptMap, it is not possible to say whether a particular ResearchElementDefinition instance should become an EvidenceVariable, an Evidence variable definition, a Group, extensions, or some combination. That uncertainty is the compatibility problem for this finding.

freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A deprecated base `ResearchElementDefinition` compatibility resource would reduce uncertainty for old instances, but would duplicate the redesigned model. An official base-level alias or normative conversion map would help, but a map by itself would not preserve R4 instances as valid R6 base instances.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing High mapping risk and Partial alternative judgment; the old report's direction is plausible, but the fresh assessment treats the missing official successor rationale as enough to make the specific adjudication unclear.

findings.title: Required PICO type and variableType code model has no direct R6 EvidenceVariable equivalent

oldState.summary: R4 required `type` as a primitive code bound required to population | exposure | outcome; `variableType` was an optional primitive code bound required to dichotomous | continuous | descriptive.

binding.description: The possible types of research elements (E.g. Population, Exposure, Outcome).

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The R4 local CodeSystem contains the PICO role codes `population`, `exposure`, and `outcome`. No same required value set appears on R6 `EvidenceVariable`.

oldState.narrativeMd: Every valid R4 `ResearchElementDefinition` had a `type` code identifying whether the element was a population, exposure, or outcome. Optional `variableType` used another required-bound primitive code for dichotomous, continuous, or descriptive variables.

newState.summary: R6 EvidenceVariable has no `type` or `variableType`; the closest fields are optional CodeableConcepts such as `handling` and `classifier` with example bindings.

binding.description: The method of handling in statistical analysis.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 `EvidenceVariable.handling` can carry boolean, continuous, dichotomous, ordinal, polychotomous, time-to-event, or not-specified handling examples. It does not encode the old required PICO role. R6 `classifier` is repeated and example-bound, so it may classify variables but is not an equivalent required role field.

facts.newValue: 0..1 CodeableConcept, example binding to boolean | continuous | dichotomous | ordinal | polychotomous | time-to-event | not-specified

facts.note: The likely variable-type successor is much less constraining and uses a different code system.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: `variableType` and R6 `handling` overlap for dichotomous and continuous variables, but `ResearchElementDefinition.type` has no direct R6 `EvidenceVariable` field. PICO role may need to be supplied by an `Evidence` variable role, classifier, or extension.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Because `type` is mandatory in every valid R4 `ResearchElementDefinition`, a naive conversion to R6 `EvidenceVariable` leaves an unknown `type` field and loses the required PICO role. Runtime code that switches on `population`, `exposure`, or `outcome` must be rewritten. R6 values in `handling` that are ordinal, polychotomous, time-to-event, or not-specified do not fit the R4 `variableType` code set.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Misclassifying population, exposure, or outcome can change the interpretation of an evidence variable or the logic that uses it in recommendations and evidence summaries.

justification.inferredGoal: Replace the fixed PICO and variable-type primitive codes with a more flexible evidence-variable classification and handling model.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain a deprecated PICO role code or add a first-class role element alongside the richer handling and classifier model.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 move toward flexible `CodeableConcept` handling and classification appears reasonable, especially because the R4 primitive `type` and `variableType` model was narrow. The break is material because every R4 instance had a required PICO role. A less-breaking base design could preserve that role, but it would create a second place to state variable role and could diverge from surrounding `Evidence` relationships, so the alternative is partial rather than clean.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best alternative would keep the old `population`/`exposure`/`outcome` role as a deprecated base element, or add an explicit R6 role element with a defined mapping from `ResearchElementDefinition.type`, while also adding the richer R6 `handling` and classifier concepts. Merely telling implementers to map the old code into `Evidence.variableDefinition.variableRole`, `classifier`, or an extension is not a backward-compatible base alternative; it is conversion policy.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: This preserves old enum switches and required role semantics, but duplicates role information that may belong in Evidence context or classifiers.

evidence.detail: R4 type is mandatory and required-bound to research-element-type.
R4 variableType is optional but required-bound to variable-type.
R6 handling is optional CodeableConcept with an example value set.
evidence.quote: boolean | continuous | dichotomous | ordinal | polychotomous | time-to-event | not-specified

evidence.detail: R6 handling examples include codes beyond the R4 variable-type code set.

examples.examplesMd: The old fragment relies on mandatory `type=outcome`. The R6 fragment uses a handling code that has no R4 `variableType` equivalent and still does not state whether the variable is a population, exposure, or outcome.

findings.narrativeMd: The classification model changed from required primitive role codes to optional CodeableConcept-based handling/classification. This breaks validators and generated code that expect a non-null enum for `type`, and it creates semantic risk because a population/exposure/outcome distinction may need to move outside the variable resource.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4 instance's `type` field cannot be carried as a same-name R6 EvidenceVariable element. Without transformation, it is invalid; with transformation, it may be lossy unless a specific target such as `Evidence.variableDefinition.variableRole`, `classifier`, or an extension is chosen. R6 handling codes also cannot all be represented in R4 `variableType`.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Define a mapping table for `population`, `exposure`, and `outcome` before migration. If variables are referenced from R6 `Evidence`, prefer preserving the role in the `Evidence` variable-definition context; otherwise use a documented classifier or extension. Map R4 `variableType=dichotomous|continuous` to R6 `handling` when clinically appropriate, and manually review `descriptive` cases.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The richer R6 handling model is useful, but removing the required PICO role without an alias or formal mapping was avoidable. A backward-compatible design could have added new handling fields while retaining a deprecated role code for cross-version conversion.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 required a primitive `type` code for population, exposure, or outcome and optionally carried `variableType`; those same paths do not exist on R6 `EvidenceVariable`. A naive field-preserving conversion is therefore invalid or semantically incomplete. However, R6 has a coherent alternative model: statistical handling belongs on `EvidenceVariable.handling`, while PICO role can be represented in `Evidence.variableDefinition.variableRole` with required population/exposure/outcome codes. Keeping the old role directly on `EvidenceVariable` would be more compatible but would duplicate role semantics that R6 appears to place in the Evidence context.
keyEvidence: R4 `ResearchElementDefinition.type` is 1..1 code with required binding to `research-element-type` codes population, exposure, outcome.
R4 `ResearchElementDefinition.variableType` is 0..1 code with required binding to dichotomous, continuous, descriptive.
R6 `EvidenceVariable.handling` is 0..1 CodeableConcept with example binding including continuous, dichotomous, ordinal, polychotomous, time-to-event, and not-specified.
R6 `Evidence.variableDefinition.variableRole` is 1..1 code with required binding including population, exposure, outcome, and covariate.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Because the R4 element is part of an FMM 0/trial-use resource, the required-code break does not by itself justify broad stability concern; the presence of an R6 role mechanism outside EvidenceVariable further softens the concern.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: old `type` and `variableType` fields are not valid same-path R6 EvidenceVariable fields; generated enum switches and reverse mapping for newer handling codes need conversion logic.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: R6 could have kept a deprecated PICO role element or added a first-class EvidenceVariable role. That would preserve old enum switches, but it would overlap with `Evidence.variableDefinition.variableRole` and could create conflicting role assertions between the variable and the evidence context.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing High impact and Partial alternative judgment; the break is real, but the report underweights the R6 `Evidence.variableDefinition.variableRole` mechanism and the low-FMM context.

findings.title: Mandatory characteristic backbone was replaced by a different optional EvidenceVariable definition model

oldState.summary: R4 required at least one characteristic, and each characteristic required definition[x].
oldState.narrativeMd: `ResearchElementDefinition.characteristic` was `1..*` and applied multiple characteristics with "and" semantics. `characteristic.definition[x]` was `1..1` and allowed `CodeableConcept`, `canonical(ValueSet)`, `Expression`, or `DataRequirement`. Optional subfields represented usage context, exclusion, UCUM unit, study-effective timing, participant-effective timing, and group aggregation.

newState.summary: R6 EvidenceVariable has no characteristic backbone; variable meaning and constraints are split across optional elements.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 `EvidenceVariable.definition` is optional `CodeableReference(Group)`. Additional optional elements include repeated `definitionModifier`, `category`, `conditional`, `dataStorage`, `timing`, `period`, `constraint`, `missingDataMeaning`, and `unacceptableDataHandling`. These fields are more granular but not path-compatible with R4 `characteristic`.

facts.newValue: EvidenceVariable.definition 0..1 CodeableReference(Group); definitionModifier.value[x] supports CodeableConcept, boolean, Quantity, Range, Period, RelativeTime, Reference(Resource), Expression, uri
No direct R6 EvidenceVariable exclude field
facts.note: Potential mappings need a definitionModifier, classifier, constraint, or extension policy.

facts.oldValue: studyEffective[x], studyEffectiveTimeFromStart, participantEffective[x], participantEffectiveTimeFromStart, groupMeasure fields
facts.newValue: EvidenceVariable.timing, period, constraint and other fields
facts.note: The split between study and participant timing is not preserved as same-path R6 elements.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Some R4 characteristic concepts have plausible R6 homes, but the model is redesigned: required repeated criteria with conjunction semantics became optional variable definition, modifiers, timing, data-storage, and constraint elements.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Every valid R4 `ResearchElementDefinition` contains at least one `characteristic`, and R6 `EvidenceVariable` does not have that element. A naive migration therefore fails validation. Generated code loses the old backbone class and choice properties. R6 can express constraints, data storage, missing-data handling, and RelativeTime semantics that R4 cannot round-trip without extensions.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Characteristics define membership criteria. Incorrectly mapping inclusion, exclusion, timing, units, or aggregation can change who is in the population or what outcome/exposure is measured.

justification.inferredGoal: Replace a compact PICO characteristic list with a richer evidence-variable model for definitions, modifiers, data storage, timing, and constraints.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep a deprecated characteristic backbone alongside R6 definition, modifier, timing, and constraint elements.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The richer R6 `EvidenceVariable` model for definitions, modifiers, data storage, timing, and constraints is a reasonable direction. Retaining the R4 `characteristic` backbone would have preserved many existing instances, but the tradeoff is substantial: validators and implementers would need rules for reconciling old criteria with new definition/modifier/constraint elements, and deprecated criteria representations could persist indefinitely. With those tradeoffs made explicit, the partial alternative does not make the breaking redesign clearly avoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A compatibility design could have kept `characteristic` as a deprecated backbone in the base R6 successor, possibly with invariants or guidance discouraging use alongside the new model. That is more backward compatible than only providing extensions or conversion guidance. However, it is incomplete because the old and new structures are not equivalent, and supporting both would introduce validation ambiguity and interoperability cost.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: This would preserve old criteria, but it creates duplicate same-resource ways to express membership, exclusion, timing, units, and constraints.

evidence.detail: R4 characteristic is mandatory and repeatable.
evidence.quote: 1..*; Multiple characteristics are applied with "and" semantics.

evidence.detail: R4 characteristic definition is mandatory with four choice types.
R6 definition is optional CodeableReference to Group.
R6 modifier value choices differ from R4 characteristic.definition[x] choices.
evidence.quote: CodeableConcept | boolean | Quantity | Range | Period | RelativeTime | Reference(Resource) | Expression | uri

examples.examplesMd: The migration example is intentionally approximate. R6 has no same-path target for `definitionCanonical` as a characteristic criterion plus `exclude=false`; a production transform needs a domain-approved representation.

findings.narrativeMd: The old membership-criteria backbone disappeared. This affects both instance validation and code generation because the R4 backbone class and its choice elements are not present in the R6 candidate. More importantly, the old conjunction and exclusion semantics must be recreated explicitly or they can be lost.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4 instance containing the required `characteristic` element is invalid as an R6 `EvidenceVariable` without a structural transform. An R6 `EvidenceVariable` can omit definition entirely or use new fields such as `dataStorage`, `constraint`, and `missingDataMeaning`, so it may not be representable as an R4 `ResearchElementDefinition` that requires `type` and `characteristic.definition[x]`.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Map each R4 characteristic separately. Preserve inclusion/exclusion, original choice type, timing basis, units, and aggregation measure in testable rules. Use extensions when no R6 core element clearly preserves semantics. Review multiple-characteristic cases because R4 explicitly used `and` semantics.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The redesign may be beneficial, but removing a mandatory backbone maximizes breakage. A compatibility period or formal extension mapping would have allowed old instances to validate or convert reproducibly while R6 implementers adopted the richer model.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The required R4 `characteristic` backbone and mandatory `characteristic.definition[x]` do not survive as same-path R6 `EvidenceVariable` content. Migration of criteria, exclusion, timing, units, and conjunction semantics needs explicit rules, so this is a real content-model and code-generation break. The redesigned R6 model is nevertheless plausibly justified: it separates variable definition, definition modifiers, timing, periods, constraints, missing-data meaning, and unacceptable-data handling in ways the compact R4 backbone could not express cleanly. Retaining the old backbone in the same base resource would create two competing ways to state membership criteria.
keyEvidence: R4 `ResearchElementDefinition.characteristic` is 1..* BackboneElement and says multiple characteristics are applied with AND semantics.
R4 `characteristic.definition[x]` is 1..1 with CodeableConcept, canonical(ValueSet), Expression, or DataRequirement choices.

R6 `EvidenceVariable.definition` is 0..1 CodeableReference(Group); `definitionModifier.value[x]` supports CodeableConcept, boolean, Quantity, Range, Period, RelativeTime, Reference(Resource), Expression, and uri.
R6 EvidenceVariable also has timing, period, constraint, missingDataMeaning, and unacceptableDataHandling elements.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 0/trial-use reduces the expectation that the mandatory R4 backbone must be preserved unchanged. The criteria are semantically important, but quick checks did not find concrete production-use evidence that would overcome the low maturity signal.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: valid R4 instances must contain `characteristic`, but R6 EvidenceVariable has no same-path backbone; generated code also loses the old backbone and choice properties.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A deprecated `characteristic` backbone in the R6 successor would preserve many old instances, but supporting it alongside definition/modifier/timing/constraint fields would require precedence and conflict rules and would perpetuate duplicate criteria representations.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing High impact and Partial alternative judgment; the migration burden is high for affected data, but the low maturity and stronger R6 model make the break proportionate.

findings.title: Several optional ResearchElementDefinition metadata and relationship fields are removed or reshaped in the likely successor

affectedLocation.oldPath: ResearchElementDefinition.subject[x] | comment | usage | jurisdiction | topic | relatedArtifact | library | subtitle
affectedLocation.newPath: EvidenceVariable.note | relatesTo | classifier and other successor fields

oldState.summary: R4 ResearchElementDefinition provided optional local metadata for subject, comments, clinical usage, jurisdiction, topic, related artifacts, and Library logic.
oldState.narrativeMd: `subject[x]` had a meaning-when-missing of Patient and could be CodeableConcept or Reference(Group). `comment` was repeated string. `usage` described clinical use. `library` referenced formal logic. `topic`, `jurisdiction`, `relatedArtifact`, and `subtitle` were also local optional fields.

newState.summary: R6 EvidenceVariable lacks several same-name fields and uses different shapes for notes and relationships.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 `EvidenceVariable.note` is repeated `Annotation`, not string `comment`. `relatesTo` is a backbone with typed target choices rather than R4 `relatedArtifact`. `classifier` may cover some topical classification. There is no same-path `subject[x]`, `usage`, `jurisdiction`, `topic`, `library`, or `subtitle` in the R6 candidate.

facts.note: Human notes can be preserved but require type and field-name conversion.
Potential mapping to relatesTo or extension requires policy.

facts.newValue: EvidenceVariable.relatesTo 0..* BackboneElement with type and target[x]

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Some information can be carried in R6 `note`, `relatesTo`, `classifier`, or extensions, but the mappings are not one-to-one and are not specified by the local package.

impact.impactRationaleMd: These fields were optional, so not every R4 instance is affected. Instances that use them cannot be converted by simple renaming, and generated code or search/indexing logic that expects those metadata paths must change. The subject default of Patient is especially easy to lose because R6 `EvidenceVariable` does not carry a same-path subject element.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Metadata loss is usually lower risk than losing criteria, but loss of subject context or formal logic references can affect interpretation in CDS or evidence applications.

justification.inferredGoal: Align EvidenceVariable with a different metadata and relationship pattern while removing ResearchElementDefinition-specific fields.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain selected deprecated metadata aliases in the base successor, especially subject, library, comment or note, and relationship fields.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Some metadata streamlining may be reasonable in a redesigned evidence model, but the local evidence does not show why removing or reshaping these optional fields was necessary at the base level. Several fields, especially `subject[x]`, `library`, and authoring comments or relationships, can affect interpretation. Because a compatibility layer could preserve common cases with moderate burden, the level of breakage is not clearly justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could retain deprecated aliases or compatibility elements for the most migration-sensitive metadata while mapping newer content to `note`, `relatesTo`, `classifier`, or other R6 fields. This would not be fully clean because duplicate metadata paths can diverge and some old fields have no exact R6 semantics. Still, relying only on project-specific mappings, extensions, or conversion tooling leaves too much data-loss risk to count as a sufficient backward-compatible alternative.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Aliases would reduce data loss for optional but meaningful metadata, but they expand the successor surface and overlap with note, relatesTo, and classifier.

evidence.detail: R4 subject[x] carries subject context and has Patient as meaning when missing.
evidence.quote: The intended subjects for the ResearchElementDefinition.

evidence.detail: R4 library references formal logic used by the ResearchElementDefinition.
R6 note is Annotation rather than R4 comment string.
R6 uses relatesTo for relationships rather than R4 relatedArtifact.

comment: Use CQL library for detailed denominator logic.

note.text: Use CQL library for detailed denominator logic.

examples.examplesMd: The example shows one plausible conversion for comments and library references. It does not preserve the old `subject[x]` default unless a separate rule or extension is added.

findings.narrativeMd: Optional does not mean unimportant. Existing R4 instances that used subject context, comments, formal logic libraries, topics, jurisdictions, or related artifacts need field-level migration decisions. The highest semantic risk in this group is losing subject context or library logic references.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4 instance using these optional paths is invalid as a naive R6 `EvidenceVariable` because the field names and datatypes differ or are absent. R6 `note` and `relatesTo` can carry some information back to R4 only with conversion rules; otherwise round-tripping can lose authoring notes, relationship types, or logic references.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Inventory optional field usage. Convert `comment` to `note.text` where appropriate. Decide whether `library` becomes `relatesTo`, an extension, or a related artifact on a surrounding resource. Preserve `subject[x]` explicitly if the R4 default Patient was relied on by CQL or other logic.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A formal metadata map would have been a low-cost compatibility measure. Without it, implementations can choose incompatible mappings for common knowledge-artifact metadata.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The optional R4 metadata and relationship fields are not path-compatible with the likely R6 successor: comments become annotations, related artifacts become `relatesTo`, and fields such as subject, usage, jurisdiction, topic, subtitle, and library lack obvious same-path homes. Instances that used these fields need migration policy, especially if they relied on the Patient subject default or on Library references for formal logic. Still, these are optional fields on an FMM 0 resource, and many can be transformed or preserved with extensions without forcing the base R6 model to carry a large set of deprecated aliases.
keyEvidence: R4 `subject[x]` is 0..1 CodeableConcept or Reference(Group) with meaningWhenMissing=Patient.
R4 `library` is 0..* canonical(Library) and `comment` is 0..* string.
R6 `EvidenceVariable.note` is 0..* Annotation and `relatesTo` is a BackboneElement relationship pattern.
No same-path R6 EvidenceVariable elements were found for several R4 fields including subject[x], usage, jurisdiction, topic, subtitle, and library.
freshReview.fmmEffect: Low FMM and trial-use status soften the concern; subject and library can matter semantically, but the affected fields are optional and no quick production-use evidence was found.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: old optional fields become invalid or absent after a naive successor conversion; some information can be remapped but not by simple path preservation.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: R6 could retain selected deprecated metadata aliases, especially subject and library, but aliases would overlap with `note`, `relatesTo`, classifiers, and extensions and could create divergent metadata. A published mapping would be useful but is not a base compatibility design.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing Medium impact and Partial alternative judgment; the optional metadata loss is real, but the fresh review sees aliases as less compelling given low FMM and duplicate-surface costs.

findings.title: Successor status is optional, creating R6-to-R4 and runtime assumptions risk

oldState.summary: R4 ResearchElementDefinition.status was mandatory and modifier.

binding.description: The lifecycle status of an artifact.

flags.isModifierReason: This is labeled as "Is Modifier" because applications should not use a retired {{title}} without due consideration

oldState.narrativeMd: Every R4 instance had to state lifecycle status. Implementers could reasonably generate a non-null enum or require status before use.

newState.summary: R6 EvidenceVariable.status is optional but remains modifier and required-bound when present.

binding.description: The lifecycle status of an artifact.

flags.isModifierReason: This is labeled as "Is Modifier" because applications should not use a retired EvidenceVariable without due consideration

newState.narrativeMd: The closest R6 successor permits missing status, with meaning when missing recorded as unknown. This is easier for R6 authoring but weaker for code that expects mandatory lifecycle state.

facts.note: Modifier status is preserved in the candidate successor.
R4 did not need a missing-status interpretation because status was mandatory.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The elements have the same lifecycle-status purpose and binding, but the match is through the candidate `EvidenceVariable` successor rather than a same-identity R6 ResearchElementDefinition.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4-to-R6 migration is not made harder by optionalizing status because all valid R4 instances already contain it. The risk is reverse mapping and runtime logic: R6 EvidenceVariable instances can omit a modifier lifecycle status, but R4 ResearchElementDefinition cannot represent a missing status without inventing one.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Lifecycle status affects whether a knowledge artifact should be used. Treating unknown status as active could be unsafe in governance workflows.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow EvidenceVariable definitions to exist without known publication status.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: No R4-to-R6 old-instance alternative is needed for this specific cardinality change; valid R4 instances already contain status.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: This finding is not an old-valid/new-invalid R4-to-R6 base-design break. R4 `ResearchElementDefinition.status` was mandatory, so any valid R4 instance can still supply status when migrated to the candidate R6 successor. Optional R6 status creates reverse-conversion and runtime-governance risk, but under the calibration rules that is not a backward-compatible alternative question for preserving R4 inputs.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Keeping `EvidenceVariable.status` mandatory would improve round-trip compatibility and lifecycle discipline, but it is a stricter R6 design choice rather than a less-breaking alternative for R4 instances. R6-to-R4 conversion policies such as defaulting missing status to `unknown` are migration mitigations, not base R6 compatibility alternatives.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: The tradeoff is mainly R6-to-R4: converters must reject or default missing status, while mandatory status would reduce R6 authoring flexibility.

evidence.detail: R4 status has min cardinality 1 and isModifier true.
R6 EvidenceVariable status has min cardinality 0, isModifier true, and meaningWhenMissing of unknown.

examples.examplesMd: The R6 fragment omits status. A reverse conversion to R4 would need to invent `status=unknown` or reject the instance.

findings.narrativeMd: The lifecycle status requirement weakens in the candidate successor. This is not an R4-to-R6 instance break, but it matters for generated models, business rules, and reverse conversion because code that assumes a non-null publication status needs to handle unknown/missing values.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: All valid R4 instances have `status`, so this specific cardinality change does not make old data invalid after a proper transform. R6 data without `status` is not directly representable in R4 `ResearchElementDefinition`, whose status is mandatory.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Preserve R4 status during forward migration. For R6-to-R4 conversion, define whether missing status becomes `unknown`, causes rejection, or is populated from governance metadata. Test retired, active, draft, unknown, and absent cases.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Making a modifier lifecycle field optional may be convenient but was not the most backward-compatible choice. Retaining mandatory status would have avoided reverse-conversion ambiguity.

freshReview.narrativeMd: This specific cardinality change does not make valid R4 data invalid in R6: every R4 `ResearchElementDefinition` already has `status`, and R6 `EvidenceVariable.status` can still carry it. The concern is mainly reverse conversion or runtime assumptions for new R6 EvidenceVariable instances that omit status. Because R6 gives missing status an explicit unknown meaning and this is not an old-valid/new-invalid R4-to-R6 break, it is not a material fresh-review concern.
keyEvidence: R4 `ResearchElementDefinition.status` is 1..1 code, required-bound to publication-status, isModifier=true, and isSummary=true.
R6 `EvidenceVariable.status` is 0..1 code, required-bound to publication-status, isModifier=true, isSummary=true, and meaningWhenMissing is `Value is unknown.`
All valid R4 instances already contain status, so forward migration can preserve the value.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 0/trial-use further lowers concern; even for mature content this would mostly be a reverse-conversion policy issue rather than an R4-to-R6 validity break.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: R6 instances may omit status and need rejection or defaulting for R4, but old R4 instances are not invalidated by the min-cardinality decrease.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Keeping R6 EvidenceVariable.status mandatory would improve lifecycle discipline and round-tripping, but it would be a stricter R6 modeling choice rather than a less-breaking design needed to preserve R4-valid instances.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing reverse-conversion observation and Not applicable alternative judgment; disagree with treating this as a medium R4-to-R6 compatibility problem.

findings.title: Summary representation changes for migrated EvidenceVariable content

oldState.summary: R4 marked experimental, effectivePeriod, and characteristic as summary elements.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 `_summary=true` views of `ResearchElementDefinition` could include `experimental`, `effectivePeriod`, and the required `characteristic` backbone, in addition to common canonical metadata.

newState.summary: R6 EvidenceVariable does not mark experimental or effectivePeriod as summary, has no characteristic, and marks different fields such as definition and versionAlgorithm[x] as summary.
newState.narrativeMd: In the candidate successor, `EvidenceVariable.definition` and `versionAlgorithm[x]` are summary, while `experimental` and `effectivePeriod` are not. This changes what clients see in summary-mode search/read responses after migration.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Summary flags were compared between the R4 assigned resource and the R6 candidate successor. Because the root artifact is removed, these are migration-surface changes rather than same-identity flag edits.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Summary flags do not normally make stored instances invalid, but they can affect REST `_summary`, generated summary views, indexing, caches, and client code that expects key research-element criteria or effective periods in summary payloads.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: A summary response that omits applicability periods or variable criteria can mislead user interfaces or caches, but full-resource retrieval remains available.

justification.inferredGoal: Tune summary-mode payloads for the redesigned EvidenceVariable resource.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep migrated applicability and variable-definition fields in summary views where they replace R4 summary content.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Summary flag changes are runtime compatibility issues rather than direct instance validation breaks. The R6 summary choices may be reasonable for the redesigned resource, but the local inputs do not explain why old summary-visible applicability and criteria signals had to disappear from summary views. A base-design alternative exists for some common cases, so the breakage is not clearly justified, though it is only partial because the old `characteristic` surface no longer has a one-to-one successor.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could mark the successor elements that carry migrated applicability or variable definition content as summary, or retain summary status for compatibility fields during a transition. Simply documenting changed `_summary` behavior is useful migration guidance but is not itself a backward-compatible base design. The tradeoff is larger summary responses and possible confusion if both old and new criteria representations are available.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: This reduces REST and client surprises, but increases summary payloads and cannot fully emulate the removed characteristic backbone without duplicate representation.

evidence.detail: R4 characteristic is summary.
R4 effectivePeriod is summary.
R6 EvidenceVariable effectivePeriod is not summary.
R6 definition is summary.

examples.examplesMd: No instance fragment is needed: summary flags affect server/client representation behavior, not instance validity.

findings.narrativeMd: The summary-view surface changes after migration. Clients that depended on summary responses to include criteria or applicability periods should not assume the R6 candidate returns equivalent data under `_summary=true`.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: FHIR instance validation is not directly affected. Runtime behavior can change in REST APIs, caches, UI list views, and generated summary DTOs. A full read can still retrieve non-summary fields if the server supports them.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Audit callers that use `_summary=true`, `_elements`, generated summary models, or search-result projections. Add tests ensuring migrated clients fetch full resources when they need effective periods, experimental flags, or detailed variable criteria.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Summary changes are often acceptable when the content model changes, but documenting them would reduce surprise. Keeping old summary-relevant semantics available in summary responses would have been more compatible.

freshReview.narrativeMd: Summary flag differences can change `_summary` projections or generated summary DTOs, but they do not affect instance validity and are secondary to the resource replacement itself. In the likely successor, `definition` is summary while `effectivePeriod` and `experimental` are not, so clients that need those fields should request full resources or explicit elements. For an FMM 0 retired resource, this is migration awareness rather than a base compatibility issue that warrants redesign.
keyEvidence: R4 marked `ResearchElementDefinition.characteristic`, `effectivePeriod`, and `experimental` as summary elements.
R6 EvidenceVariable marks `definition` and `versionAlgorithm[x]` as summary, while `effectivePeriod` and `experimental` are not summary.
Summary flags affect REST/client projections, not whether a resource instance validates.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 0/trial-use makes summary projection continuity a weak stability concern, especially because no concrete production use of `_summary` for this resource was found.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: metadata/tooling: summary projections, caches, or generated summary views may change, but base instance validation and full-resource retrieval are unaffected.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: R6 could mark more successor fields as summary or retain summary-compatible deprecated fields, but that would increase payload size and still could not emulate the removed characteristic backbone without duplicate representation.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: disagree with the existing Medium runtime impact and Partial alternative judgment; the fresh review treats this as low-risk projection/tooling churn, not a meaningful compatibility problem.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: For the closest successor comparison, lifecycle `status` remains `isModifier=true`. Inherited `modifierExtension` behavior is excluded as a base-artifact issue.
No local R4 `ResearchElementDefinition` element or inspected R6 `EvidenceVariable` successor element used fixed, pattern, or default values that would create an additional local fixed-value break.

No local slicing definitions were found in the R4 assigned resource or the R6 `EvidenceVariable` candidate successor. The content-model break is element restructuring, not slice discriminator or slice-rule change.

No ElementDefinition-level `minValue`, `maxValue`, `maxLength`, or regex value limits were identified on local R4 `ResearchElementDefinition` elements. R6 `EvidenceVariable.constraint` introduces data-value constraint elements, but those are model content, not ElementDefinition value-limit changes on the old artifact.

Reference target changes inside the successor model were considered in findings for characteristic and metadata migration. No same-identity R6 `ResearchElementDefinition` reference targets exist to compare directly.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Closest successor has higher maturity/status metadata
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The status and maturity of R6 `EvidenceVariable` do not make R4 instances invalid by themselves; the breaking issue is the removal of `ResearchElementDefinition`.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: R4 `ResearchElementDefinition` was draft/trial-use/FMM 0. R6 `EvidenceVariable` is active with standards-status normative and FMM 1 in the inspected StructureDefinition. This may explain willingness to redesign but does not provide conversion rules.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.path: EvidenceVariable.versionAlgorithm[x] | citeAs | recorder | actual | dataStorage | missingDataMeaning | unacceptableDataHandling
nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 EvidenceVariable adds optional expressive fields
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: Optional additions to the likely successor do not invalidate R4 content after a proper transform.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: These fields can improve R6 representations, but R6 instances using them may not round-trip to R4 `ResearchElementDefinition` without extensions or loss.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 EvidenceVariable uses changed warning constraints for canonical name and URL
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The constraints are warnings, not error-level validation requirements, and apply to the candidate successor rather than a same-name ResearchElementDefinition resource.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: R4 `ResearchElementDefinition` had warning `red-0` for code-generation-friendly names. R6 `EvidenceVariable` has warning `cnl-0` requiring a stricter name regex when present and `cnl-1` warning that URL should not contain `|`, `#`, or spaces. Systems treating warnings as errors should test names and URLs.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: R6 `EvidenceVariable` is the closest candidate migration destination. Its own R4-to-R6 breaking changes should be coordinated with this removal report before defining a migration.
R6 `Evidence` may carry variable roles and relationships that preserve R4 PICO role semantics better than `EvidenceVariable` alone.
R4 `ResearchDefinition` referenced `ResearchElementDefinition` for population/exposure/outcome. Its removal and migration strategy are tightly coupled with this artifact.
A formal mapping is needed for `type`, `variableType`, `characteristic.definition[x]`, exclusion, timing, UCUM units, group-measure, subject, library, and related-artifact metadata.
Terminology review should decide how R4 required codes map to R6 example-bound CodeableConcepts and whether extensions or local code systems are needed.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: The analysis did not have an official R4-to-R6 diff, ballot disposition, or change note explaining whether `ResearchElementDefinition` was deleted, merged, or replaced by a specific pattern.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: An HL7 migration note or official diff that states the intended successor and rationale.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No authoritative ConceptMap or conversion guide was found for mapping R4 `ResearchElementDefinition` fields to R6 `EvidenceVariable`, `Evidence`, `Group`, or extensions.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: An official cross-version map with examples for population, exposure, outcome, variable type, criteria, exclusion, timing, units, and metadata.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: Terminology analysis used local ValueSet and CodeSystem definitions, not full terminology-server expansions or external code-system versions.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Run terminology expansions for the R4 and R6 value sets, including UCUM and any external systems, and compare mapped code semantics.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: Rendered narrative specification pages and examples were not inspected. Those pages might clarify intended migration patterns, especially around `EvidenceVariable` and `Evidence`.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Review the official R4 and R6 narrative pages, examples, and ballot notes for the evidence domain.
